summary: On the Get started questions, a small link under the pay box now says "I only know what reaches my bank". Type one paycheck's take-home and the page works out your pay before tax, allowing for your 401(k) share, Social Security and Medicare tax, federal tax held back and your state's flat rule. The result is marked as worked out, so it updates if your 401(k) share changes.
points: Pay is saved as a guess that follows your 401(k) share
Going back reopens the box as you typed it
A pay guess now reopens blank, shown in gray

summary: A home or education goal left blank on question 7b no longer quietly counts as $0. It now takes our figure, the typical down payment in your state or the Education page's own figure for your children, shown in gray and saved as a guess. A trip or "something else" left blank stays at 0 and the summary asks you to add an amount.
points: Older plans are offered the two amounts on Fill in what you skipped
Gray marks the figure as our guess, not yours
numbers: 2 goal types now get a starting amount

summary: On question 3, if you pick a stop age before full retirement age, the page now says when Social Security pays in full and that your savings carry the years in between. A button moves your stop age to that age if you want. Your chosen stop age stays as you set it.
points: Message appears only for stops before full retirement age
One tap moves the stop age to full retirement age
numbers: 1 new message and 1 button on question 3

summary: "Estimate it for me" on question 3 now saves its Social Security figure as our guess, so it moves when your pay changes, whether typed on Income or from our pay guess. A figure you typed on the Social Security page stays yours. Plans saved earlier keep their figure until you accept the better guess.
points: Older plans are left alone until you accept
numbers: 65 new test lines on the question flow

summary: In the pay-off-what-I-owe guide, the rate and payment step now counts as done once every loan and card has a rate and a payment, whether you typed them or we guessed them. Its words tell you where to type the real ones. A debt with no rate at all keeps the step open.
points: Guessed rates count as filled in
A debt with no rate keeps the step open

summary: The last step on the dashboard checklist is now Look over our guesses and links to the Our guesses for you page. It is done once you tap "These look fine", or when none of the big figures is our guess. Marking assumptions reviewed no longer ticks it.
points: Step stays in the same place, so the one next step is unchanged

summary: The Get started summary no longer says "Type its rate on the State tax page" where we can already work the tax out. It now shows only where the state's tax cannot be worked out, not for flat-rate states like Arizona, states with no wage tax, when you typed a rate or last year's return, or outside the U.S.
points: Hidden for flat-rate and no-tax states
Hidden when you gave a rate or a return
